title: Shared temperature-dependent heat-to-creep material contract
purpose: Verify that one thermoelastic material asset and one accepted thermal history drive heat transfer, Arrhenius creep rate, temperature-dependent elastic response, thermal strain, restart identity, and structured energy evidence.
physics: Sequential three-dimensional transient heat transfer and small-strain thermoelastic Arrhenius power-law creep

execution.evidence: A transient heat Step captures accepted finite-element temperature states. The global creep Step consumes the same physical clock and thermoelastic property object at its quadrature identity; a second test compares continuous and restarted temperature-dependent E(T) paths.

observables: Accepted thermal-history times and active creep time
Integration-point temperature extrema and nonuniform CEEQ
TEMP, CE, CEEQ, S, MISES, RF and recovered cell fields
Elastic energy, creep dissipation, internal energy, external work channels and mechanical energy residual
acceptance: The heat and creep procedures share one inspectable thermoelastic property object.
Every attempted creep increment samples positive kelvin temperature at the constitutive quadrature identity.
Rollback and checkpoint reconstruction evaluate stress and tangent at the accepted temperature without advancing fictitious creep time.
The completed result retains temperature, constitutive state and energy histories.
limitations: This internal component integration test is not an external power-plant component validation.
The route is sequential one-way coupling; mechanical dissipation is not fed back into heat transfer.
Thermal-expansion tables are treated as secant coefficients relative to the declared reference temperature.
